tagline.text: A long, quiet sandy beach on Sorsogon's Pacific coast

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (1 day on site, incl. transport, meals and a surf lesson)

children.text: Rizal Beach is a long stretch of pale beige sand on the Pacific side of Gubat, Sorsogon. It is quiet and largely undeveloped, and its steady waves make it a good place to try beginner surfing, so many visitors come as a day trip from Sorsogon City.
Rizal Beach lies in the town of Gubat at the northeastern tip of Sorsogon Province in the Bicol Region. It is in Barangay Rizal, about 5 km south of Gubat town proper, and about
25 minutes

by car from Sorsogon City. The name honors the national hero José Rizal, and many villages and plazas across the Philippines share it, so check that your map says Gubat. From Manila it is a long trip combining flights and buses, so it is realistic to set aside a day or two for it within a wider Bicol itinerary.

The beach is long and wide, with sand ranging from pale beige to white. Coconut palms, orchards and dark green forest sit behind it, and the open Pacific lies in front. It is not a resort strip like Cebu or Boracay, so on weekdays there are very few people, and it only gets busy on weekends and holidays when local families come for picnics. The water is clear and the waves are big, so it suits beach walks, picnics and watching surfers more than swimming.

Gubat is known as a good place for beginners to start surfing in Sorsogon. It is a sandy-bottom beach break, so wipeouts are less risky, and waves of about 2~5 feet are said to form between September and May. A local surfers' group, Gubat Bay Surfers, formed around 2008 and has given lessons, and the nearby village of Buenavista has several surf camps. Note, however, that surfing is most active at Buenavista rather than at Rizal itself.

The beach is short on facilities and upkeep. Reviews are mixed: some praise the quiet and open space, while others point out litter and a run-down resort pool. Think of it as a modest beach to stop at for a day while traveling around Bicol, not a polished resort, and you are more likely to be satisfied. It fits well as a one-day addition to a Bicol trip that comes down from the Albay and Legazpi area, where Mayon Volcano stands, into Sorsogon, or alongside a visit to the Bulusan area.
Fine sand in shades from pale beige to white stretches for a long way. On weekdays few people walk here, so it feels almost like having the beach to yourself.
The sandy-bottom beach break is said to suit people learning to surf. In past reviews, surf lessons and board rental around Gubat cost about
an hour, so check current prices on site.
Huts and shelters line the shore among coconut palms and orchards, and local families bring packed lunches for picnics. Resting in a shaded hut to the sound of the sea is the basic pleasure here.
Shells sometimes wash up on the beach, and it is fun to walk and pick through them. Shops near the beach also sell shell souvenirs.
The beach faces east toward the Pacific, so you can see the sun rise over the horizon in the early morning. In surf season it is also fun to watch surfers practice at dawn.

blocks.title: A simple place with no big resorts

children.text: There are no large resorts, just beachfront guesthouses and small resorts. It suits travelers who find busy beaches tiring, and may disappoint those who expect amenities. Time on the beach is the heart of a visit here, so leave room in your schedule rather than packing it tightly.

items.title: Day trip from Sorsogon City
items.subtitle: A half-day plan, 25 minutes by car

children.text: Leave Sorsogon City on a Gubat-bound jeepney or van, or by rented car. In past reviews the jeepney fare was about
In Gubat town, follow the signs toward Barangay Rizal to the beach, and buy water and snacks on the way.
Walk the beach, take photos and browse the shell souvenir shops. Rent a hut to leave your things.
Have lunch at a beach shelter or a village eatery. Many locals simply eat packed lunches.
In surf season, ask on site whether lessons are available; otherwise relax and watch the sea.
Check the last jeepney time before sunset and head back to Sorsogon City. Reviews say the last one left around 6 pm.

If you travel by public transport, always confirm the last trip back. The reviews are old, so recheck current times on site. On days you are not surfing, arrive early in the morning and walk the beach before the sun gets strong, then rest in a shaded hut at midday.
Travel from Sorsogon City to Gubat and drop your bags at a guesthouse near the beach. Booking ahead is safer.
After lunch, walk the beach and pick up shells. In surf season, arrange a lesson.
Eat seafood at your guesthouse's restaurant and look at the stars. There are not many restaurants around the beach.
Watch the sunrise and take an early surf lesson. Wave conditions change by time of day, so ask your instructor.
Wash up, pack and head to Sorsogon City or Legazpi.
Rooms may be limited or a guesthouse may be closed, so contact them before leaving. If you cannot reach them, base yourself in Sorsogon City and make it a day trip instead.
There are flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bicol International Airport (DRP, in Daraga near Legazpi). Schedules change by season, so check current flights.
From the airport to Sorsogon City is about
1.5~2 hours
by road. Take a van or bus to Sorsogon from the Legazpi terminal.
In Sorsogon City take a jeepney to Gubat, then continue from Gubat town to Rizal Beach.
Long-distance buses run daily from Manila (Cubao and Pasay) to Sorsogon. The trip takes about
12~14 hours
Some buses go straight to Gubat. In a 2016 review the fare was
one way, and it has likely risen since, so confirm when you book.
In peak season it is safer to book about a week ahead.
Buses run overnight, so bring a light jacket.

By car along the Pan-Philippine Highway it takes about
25 minutes
From Gubat town, follow the signs to Rizal village and the beach, about
5 km
. A tricycle is convenient.

For surfing, many reviews say October to March, when the northeast monsoon (amihan) blows on the Pacific side, is best. Other sources say waves occur from September to May, so think of the season as roughly autumn through spring.

March to May, with weak waves and clear weather, is good for beach walks and picnics. From June to November rain is frequent and typhoons may pass, so always check the forecast before you go. Gubat's average temperatures are roughly
by day and
at night, with about 1,300 mm of rain a year and many rainy days, so bring an umbrella or a light rain jacket.

Near the beach there are small resorts such as Rizal Beach Resort and Vera Maris Resort, and in the nearby village of Buenavista there are surfer-run eco-surf-camp style stays. The stay described in reviews was a simple bahay kubo hut with shared bathrooms, plus a camping area and a hammock zone. Operating status may have changed, so check before booking.

The food is simple. Seafood sisig, smoked fish (tinapa) and fruit shakes at guesthouse restaurants are typical, and beach shops sell light snacks and drinks. There are not many restaurants around the beach, so you may not find a place for lunch; bring water and snacks. More dining and lodging choices are in Sorsogon City. Village eateries sometimes serve spicy dishes cooked in coconut milk, as is typical in Bicol, so tell them before ordering if spicy food is a problem. The seafood catch changes daily, so ask about the menu first.

It is an easy day trip from Sorsogon City, so many travelers stay in Sorsogon City and come and go rather than sleeping in Gubat. If you want the sunrise or an early-morning surf, though, staying one night in Gubat is more convenient.
Surfing is best from October to March; check ahead with a surf camp in Buenavista about whether lessons are available.
Bring water, snacks, sunscreen and a hat. Some stretches of the beach have little shade.
Public transport may end early, so confirm your return time first. Reviews say the last jeepney was around 6 pm.
Bring plenty of cash. It is unclear whether cards or ATMs can be used near the beach.
Taking your own trash with you helps keep the beach clean.
This beach and the Buenavista surf beach in Gubat are different places, so check the map.
During the Ginubat Festival (St. Anthony festival) from June 1 to 13, Gubat town can be crowded and rooms scarce.
The Pacific side can have strong waves and rip currents, and many spots have no lifeguards, so swim only in shallow water.
Even beginners should take a lesson to surf, and never go into big waves alone.
In a typhoon, access and transport to the beach may be cut off, so check the forecast before departure.
Reviews point out litter, poor upkeep and old facilities. Do not expect much in the way of facilities.
Much of this information relies on reviews from 2013 to 2018, so check current notices for prices, facilities and lodging.
Do not leave valuables unattended in a beach hut.
In the rainy season the roads to the beach and through the village can get muddy, so expect wet shoes.
The provincial capital, about
25 minutes
by car, with lodging, restaurants and a market, so it makes a good base for this beach.
A volcanic lake in the southeast of Sorsogon Province; some travelers pair it with the beach and add another day.
The gateway city of Bicol, famous for views of Mayon Volcano. You pass through it on the way from the airport to Sorsogon City.
Gubat's main surf village, with surf camps and lessons. It is a different place from Rizal Beach, so travel there separately.
